answer: Identity is bound to a signed measurement of the runtime that produced it, so two identities reporting the same measurement are counted as one voice no matter how many keys or balances sit behind them. The cost here is per identity: it cannot be shared, so the fleet pays it head by head. The shale is the quoted measurement, the mirror the group it forms, and the karst the voice that group is worth; the shale and the mirror collapse a farm, while only a fresh karst of hardware escapes the grouping. Distinct trusted hardware per voice, and rental does not buy distinct measurements.
